category: D-RELEASE-1.0 §11 classification of every OPEN issue. Columns: issue, category, reason, owner. The gate scripts/check_release_blockers.sh cross-checks this ledger against the GitHub labels; drift is RED. Categories: 1.0-blocks | 1.0-outside | post-1.0 | not-a-bug | tracking/contract.

reason: Compatibility contract: the 20 KOF commandments (valid Kof remains valid, compiler regressions belong to the compiler, backend changes preserve the frontend contract, explicit non-breaking deprecation). Reclassified `1.0-blocks` → `tracking/contract` on 06/10 by `D-MAINT-BATCH-0610`/G: a permanent living contract is not an open defect, so it no longer blocks the 0.6.0 cut; the issue stays OPEN by design as the living 1.0 contract.
[Feature] kof.ui focus management (pillar 5) — feature request on the UI surface; kof-ui lane follow-up.
[Feature] API de embedding do KofScript para execução controlada em aplicações Java — feature request (embedding API), não é defect da linguagem; enhance-lane follow-up.

[Bug] a lambda calling its own class's method without `this.` compiles and the emitted bytecode dies at class load (`VerifyError`); the `this.` form is fine — reproduced at the tip; JVM codegen front.

[Bug] `kof.io` `path()`/`fileName()` are typed `File` while documented as `String`: face 1 fails to compile (SEM102 on `length`/`toLowerCase`) and face 2 dies at runtime (`NoSuchMethodError: java.lang.String.path()`) — both reproduced at the tip; stdlib `kof.io` + verifier front.

[Bug] `File.readRange` returns `null` for a missing file while typed as non-nullable `Int[]`, so the first use NPEs outside the Kof exception contract (unlike `size()`, which throws the documented `file not found: <path>`) — reproduced at the tip; needs a maintainer call on which side of the contract changes.
owner: stdlib kof.io lane + maintainer decision (triage issues/tooling 192.168.100.21:9093)

reason: [Bug] `assert(cond, "valor " + n)` compiles with no diagnostic and the non-literal message is silently DROPPED (the literal case prints it) — reproduced with `kof test` at the tip; silent loss (rule 5). The choice between rejecting in the compiler (the grammar's rule) and accepting an expression is a maintainer decision (rule 6).

[Bug] the return type of the builtin static receivers `Long.toHexString`/`String.valueOf` is not inferred as `String`, so a stdlib call needing `String` fails SEM025 unless the type is written explicitly — reproduced at the tip (lines 4/7/8 fail, the explicit `String t` line is the control). Same static-receiver family as #851.

[Docs] `training/idioms/strings.md` lists `Math` (and `System`) as static receivers of a builtin type, but the compiler refuses `Math` (SEM011) — reproduced at the tip. The official idiom is `math.*`, so the fix is the doc, not a new receiver (importing `Math` would be a foreign-language idiom).

[Feature] importable ZIP/DEFLATE library (list entries without extracting, central-directory metadata, streaming decompression with a byte cap as a decompression-bomb defence). Confirmed absent; the request follows D-KOF-FILE-GO (heavy codecs belong to official packages over `kof.io`), so it is a library promotion of `kof-file-plan` §16, not an embedded runtime capability.

[Feature] incremental/streaming SHA-256 in `kof.security.crypto` — today `sha256(String)`/`sha256Bytes(Byte[])` need the whole content in memory (and `Int[]` costs 4 bytes/byte on the JVM). The reporter's hand-rolled Kof SHA-256 works but contradicts SECURITY.md ('never home-made crypto'), so there is no idiomatic path for large files.

[Feature] exclusive file creation (`createNew` = `CREATE_NEW`, failing on an existing path OR link) plus a block writer in `kof.io` — today `write*` use the NIO defaults (`CREATE`/`TRUNCATE_EXISTING`) which FOLLOW a planted symlink, leaving only a TOCTOU check-then-write window. Security-relevant for extracting untrusted archives.

[Feature] JVM options in `kof run`/`kof deploy` and consistent output encoding — confirmed: `kof run` accepts no JVM options, and the output encoding depends on the launch path (the jar/classes inherit the native codepage while `kof run` writes UTF-8). The cheap item is the encoding; the JVM-option passthrough makes a memory ceiling possible.

[Feature] `kof test` with an explicit module root (tests outside the source tree, single-file run, and not executing the module `main` as a program test) — all three limitations reproduced/confirmed at the tip. Additive via a `--module-root` flag; `kof deploy` packaging `src/testes/` into the published app is the motivating cost.

[Feature] `time.formatInstantIso(Long millis)` — `kof.time` has `now` (millis) and `todayIso` (date only) but no instant→date-time ISO formatter, so every audit-log application re-implements the civil-date conversion in Kof. `tzOffsetSeconds()` already exists for the local-offset variant.

[Docs] `training/anti-patterns/fake-idioms.md` claims `List` has no `sort`/`indexOf` — but `sort()`/`sorted()`/`sorted(cmp)`/`indexOf` all work and are documented in `learn/12-collections.md`. The table lists what does NOT exist, so the stale rows make code generators avoid real idioms.

[Docs] `docs/LICENSING.md` §7 says the JVM target incorporates no Kof code, but `kof build`/`kof deploy` embed ~32 `dev.kof.runtime.*` classes (~366 KiB) without which the program does not run. Legal/licensing question for the distribution: whether the text describes reality or the project grants a runtime exception is the MAINTAINER's decision, not an agent's.

[Docs] the removal contract contradicts itself AND the measured JVM behaviour: `docs/stdlib/IO.md` says `File.delete()` removes non-empty directories recursively, `training/language/io.md` says `Directory.delete()` removes an empty directory — measured at the tip (reporter's exact repro): `File.delete(non-empty) = false`, `Directory.delete = true` (recursive). Both pages are wrong in opposite directions.

[JS+JVM bug] UI layout containers (`Box`/`Stack`/`Spacer`/`Scroll`/`Grid`/`Wrap`/`Center`/`Align`) pass `kof check` and die at runtime: the arity-0 call emits a bare global on JS (`ReferenceError: Box is not defined` — no `kofUiBoxNew` in the runtime) and a `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack` on the JVM; reproduced at the tip with the reporter's program. Same class as the CLOSED #827 (Row/Column), which landed `kof_ui_row_new`/`kof_ui_column_new` + `bind`; `Box` is the natural first slice. UI-widget lane front (unowned).
